 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever, WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson of the Las Vegas Aces and 2026 Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx earned 2026 All-WNBA First Team selections, which the league announced ahead of Saturday's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals .
 Miles was the only first-timer among the First Team this season, while Clark and Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell were each named for the second time. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart was a First Team choice for the seventh time in her career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Atlanta Dream teammates Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard, along with Shakira Austin of the Washington Mystics, were Second Team selections for the first time in their careers.
 2026 All-WNBA selections
 First Team
 A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces
Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx
Kelsey Mitchell, Indiana Fever
Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty
Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever
 Wilson, who claimed her third straight WNBA MVP award this season, was named a First Team selection for the sixth time. Stewart was top 10 this season in scoring (20.8 points per game), rebounds (8.3) and blocks (1.3) while playing the fourth-most minutes per night (33).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Miles made a quick impact in her first season. The rookie of the year was a unanimous choice for the award and finished second behind Wilson in MVP voting. In 40 games, the Lynx guard averaged 19.8 points, 6 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 0.6 blocks per game while shooting 49.2% from the field and 38.8% from 3.
 Mitchell and Clark finished third and fourth in MVP voting. Mitchell set several WNBA regular-season records for most points (1,086), 3-pointers (135), 10-plus point games (44), and 20-plus point games (35). Clark had an historic season of her own, becoming the first WNBA player to finish in the top three in points (22.3 per game) and assists (8.3 per game).
 Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream reacts during the second quarter in game three of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.
 (Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images) Second Team
 Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings
Jackie Young, Los Angeles Sparks
Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream
Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream
Shakira Austin, Washington Mystics
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Reese, already named the Defensive Player of the Year, also led the WNBA in rebounding, becoming the first player ever to grab at least 500 boards in a season (521). She also set the record for double-doubles with 32 and is just the eighth player ever to average 15-10 in a season. Howard led the WNBA in steals, ranked second in 3-pointers and was the first player ever to average at least three 3-pointers and two steals per game in a season.
 Austin was top 10 in MVP voting, finished fourth for Defensive Player of the Year and was five votes shy of winning Most Improved Player. She nearly averaged a double-double for the Mystics with 17 points and 9.5 rebounds per game — making her one of three players to average 17-9 this season along with Wilson and Nneka Ogwumike.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bueckers, a Second Team pick last year, only got better in her second WNBA season. The Wings guard ranked top 10 in points (20.9 per game), assists (5.9) and 3-point percentage (41%) a season after taking home Rookie of the Year.
 The veteran Young posted a career-high 18.9 points and dished out 6.8 assists in 2026 for the Aces, putting her in the top 10 league-wide. This is her third Second Team selection.
